scams.name: Windsor Castle Admission Third-Party Reseller Inflation
scams.description: Windsor Castle is the world's oldest and largest inhabited castle (still an official royal residence) and Windsor's #1 tourist attraction. Official admission is £33.50 adult, £20 concessions (age 60+), £18.50 children direct at rct.uk (the Royal Collection Trust site — the ONLY legitimate source) — payable card-only at the gate, with timed-entry slots in peak season (Easter-September). The significant price point and royal-heritage appeal create a robust third-party reseller market that exploits tourists unfamiliar with the official booking channel. Traveler reports widely document the cross-attraction pattern where Viator and GetYourGuide sell tickets at multiples of the face value, and 2025 discussions document the current Windsor-specific pricing confusion and reinforce the need to book direct. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers: (1) third-party reseller sites (windsor-castle-tickets.com, windsor-royal-castle.co.uk, and SEO-gamed variants) buy Google ads above rct.uk; (2) these resellers display £33.50 or £35 prominently, then add £4-£8 'booking fee' + £2-£5 'priority entry' + £10-£15 'audio guide' (which is INCLUDED free at official admission) at checkout, bringing final price to £49-£62 for the same £33.50 ticket; (3) some resellers sell 'Windsor + Changing of the Guard premium view' at £75-£99 — the Changing of the Guard is FREE to watch from outside the castle (weather permitting) so this premium 'view' is fabricated; (4) 'Windsor VIP Experience' tickets at £129-£199 claim 'behind the scenes access' that doesn't exist — Windsor Castle does NOT offer behind-the-scenes tours to retail consumers; (5) combo bundles 'Windsor + Hampton Court + Tower of London' at £149-£229 per person via third parties (direct booking: Windsor £33.50 + Hampton Court £29.50 + Tower £34.80 = £97.80 for all three); (6) older travelers age 60+ are entitled to the 'Senior' concession (£20 vs £33.50 adult) — resellers don't apply this discount automatically, so you overpay by £13.50 per ticket; (7) the Royal Collection Trust membership (£55/year adult, £85 joint) gives unlimited free entry to Windsor, Buckingham Palace, Hampton Court, Kensington Palace, Holyroodhouse (Edinburgh) — excellent value for older travelers planning multiple royal sites; (8) St George's Chapel (inside the castle, burial place of Queen Elizabeth II) is included in the £33.50 ticket but closed Sundays — verify your visit date at rct.uk. For older travelers visiting Windsor Castle: (1) book tickets ONLY at rct.uk (the Royal Collection Trust official site) — check the URL manually; (2) claim the Senior concession (£20 for age 60+) — if you're older than 60, this saves £13.50 per ticket over the adult £33.50; (3) the audio guide is INCLUDED free at official admission — refuse any reseller 'audio guide upgrade' at £10-£15; (4) for peak season (Easter-September), book timed entry 1-3 weeks ahead; off-season can be walk-up; (5) refuse ALL 'Windsor VIP Experience' packages at £129-£199 — Windsor Castle doesn't offer retail behind-the-scenes tours; (6) for combo bundles, book each site directly — Windsor (£33.50, senior £20) + Hampton Court (£29.50) + Tower of London (£34.80) = £97.80 adult / £66.50 senior, vs £149-£229 via third parties; (7) for Changing of the Guard, it's FREE to watch from outside the castle on the public pavement — refuse all 'premium view' tickets, but note it runs on alternate days only (check royal.uk) and is cancelled in heavy rain; (8) consider Royal Collection Trust Membership at £55/year (individual) for unlimited entry across 5 royal sites — pays off if you visit 2+ during UK trip; (9) St George's Chapel (where Queen Elizabeth II is buried) is included but closed on Sundays; (10) for UK Senior Railcard holders (£30/year, 60+), GWR direct train London Paddington to Slough (15 min, £9-14 off-peak) + Great Western to Windsor & Eton Central (10 min, change at Slough) is the cheapest transport.
scams.avoidance: Book tickets ONLY at rct.uk (Royal Collection Trust official site) — check URL manually Claim Senior concession (£20 for age 60+) — saves £13.50 per ticket Audio guide is INCLUDED free — refuse 'audio guide upgrade' at £10-£15 For combo sites, book each directly: Windsor + Hampton Court + Tower = £97.80 adult / £66.50 senior Consider Royal Collection Trust Membership at £55/year for unlimited entry to 5 royal sites
scams.location: Windsor Castle main entrance (Castle Hill, Windsor), third-party reseller websites — targeting Windsor Castle's £33.50 admission

scams.name: Windsor Changing of the Guard 'Premium View' Tour Upsell
scams.description: Windsor Castle's Changing of the Guard ceremony is one of the UK's most-watched royal traditions — running alternating days (typically Tue/Thu/Sat April-July, Mon-Sat August, limited winter schedule) at 11:00 AM when weather permits. The ceremony is FREE to watch from the Castle Hill pavement and St George's Gate approach — no ticket required. Despite the free nature, third-party operators sell 'Windsor Changing of the Guard Premium View' tours at £39-£99 per person that either don't provide access that isn't already public OR sell Windsor Castle admission (the only paid-access angle) at 2x markup. Community consensus is simple: 'just stand on Castle Hill for free.' Other community discussions reinforce the free nature and schedule confusion, and 2025 reports name the specific overpricing pattern. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers: (1) Changing of the Guard takes place at Windsor Castle's Upper Ward — INSIDE the castle, visible only if you've paid £33.50 admission; (2) BUT the guards PROCESSION to and from the castle via Castle Hill and the High Street is visible for FREE from the public pavement; (3) third-party tour operators sell 'Premium View + Changing of the Guard' at £39-£99 per person — typically delivering: either public-pavement viewing (which is free) OR Windsor Castle admission at markup; (4) the 'VIP Guard Ceremony Access' at £99-£249 claims 'behind the ropes' access that doesn't exist — all public viewing is either from the free pavement or the general-admission Upper Ward with £33.50 ticket; (5) schedule variability is the hook — operators sell 'guaranteed access' on dates when the ceremony isn't running (weather-dependent, alternate-days pattern); (6) some operators bundle 'Changing of the Guard + Castle Admission + Long Walk photo package' at £89-£149 — the Long Walk is a FREE public park; (7) older travelers unfamiliar with UK military-pageant traditions often don't realize the ceremony is free from the pavement — vendors exploit this; (8) the Windsor ceremony is similar to but smaller than Buckingham Palace's — tourists often confuse the two; (9) Royal.uk (the official royal website) publishes the Changing of the Guard schedule for both sites. For older travelers wanting to see Changing of the Guard at Windsor: (1) arrive at Windsor Castle Hill by 10:30 AM for the 11:00 AM ceremony (weather permitting) on the scheduled days (check royal.uk); (2) stand on the public pavement at Castle Hill or the High Street — the guards PROCESSION is fully visible for FREE; (3) for ceremony views INSIDE the Upper Ward, buy Windsor Castle admission (£33.50, or £20 senior) at rct.uk — this gets you the full ceremony AND Windsor Castle tour; (4) refuse ALL 'Changing of the Guard Premium View' tours at £39-£99 — you're paying for pavement access that's free; (5) refuse 'VIP Guard Ceremony Access' at £99-£249 — no such behind-the-ropes access exists; (6) verify the ceremony IS running — check royal.uk the night before for weather/schedule; (7) for older travelers who want to see the ceremony without crowds, 10:00 AM arrival for the 11:00 ceremony guarantees a good pavement spot; (8) after the ceremony, the Long Walk (free public park stretching from the castle to the Copper Horse statue) is a lovely 1.5-mile walk with castle views — free; (9) if you're already in London, the Buckingham Palace Changing of the Guard is often more accessible (more regular schedule, larger viewing areas) — royal.uk shows both schedules; (10) for older travelers with mobility concerns, the Castle Hill pavement has limited seating — arrive early or bring a folding stool.
scams.avoidance: Stand on the public Castle Hill pavement — the guards PROCESSION is FREE to view For ceremony INSIDE Upper Ward, buy Windsor Castle admission at rct.uk (£33.50 / £20 senior) Refuse ALL 'Premium View' tours at £39-£99 — pavement viewing is already free Verify ceremony IS running at royal.uk the night before (weather/alternate-days pattern) Long Walk after ceremony is a free public park — 1.5-mile walk with castle views
scams.location: Windsor Castle Upper Ward, Castle Hill pavement, State Entrance — targeting the Changing of the Guard free public ceremony

scams.name: Windsor Train-Station Confusion & Wrong-Station Upsell
scams.description: Windsor has TWO separate railway stations — Windsor & Eton Central (terminates GWR trains from London Paddington via Slough) and Windsor & Eton Riverside (terminates SWR trains from London Waterloo direct). They are 400 meters apart but served by different train operators at different pricing. This routing complexity creates confusion that tourists pay premium to resolve. Traveler reports document the Richmond → Windsor & Eton Riverside vs Paddington → Slough → Windsor & Eton Central split, and note: 'You can't yet use contactless on the trains from Waterloo station to Windsor and Eton Riverside' — a key detail older tourists miss. 2025 community discussions reinforce the Slough/Central detail and document the change-at-Slough pattern. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers: (1) the two options from London: London Waterloo → Windsor & Eton Riverside (direct, 55 min, £11-£15 off-peak via SWR) OR London Paddington → Slough → Windsor & Eton Central (55-65 min with change, £9-£14 off-peak via GWR + Great Western); (2) contactless tap-pay is NOT available on the SWR Waterloo-Riverside route — this catches out tourists expecting to use their Oyster/contactless card; (3) contactless IS available on the GWR Paddington-Slough-Central route; (4) third-party tour operators sell 'Windsor Rail + Castle' packages at £65-£89 per person — the train portion is the £11-£15 fare, so you're overpaying £30-£75 for the 'bundled' booking; (5) 'Windsor + Eton Riverside transfer service' at £25-£45 per person is sold by unlicensed operators — actual taxi from Windsor & Eton Central to Windsor & Eton Riverside is 3-4 minute walk, no taxi needed; (6) some resellers sell 'London-Windsor-Hampton Court' combo rail tickets at £79-£119 that cover standard GWR journeys legitimately bookable at gwr.com for £35-£55; (7) UK Senior Railcard (£30/year, 60+) gives 34% off all GWR and SWR fares — £11-£15 becomes £7.50-£10; (8) the BritRail Pass for international tourists covers both routes but costs £39-£69 per day — cheaper per-trip only if you're making 3+ UK rail trips that day. For older travelers traveling London-Windsor: (1) if you hold an Oyster card or contactless card, use the GWR route via London Paddington → Slough → Windsor & Eton Central (contactless tap-and-go works); (2) if pre-booking tickets, use SWR direct from London Waterloo → Windsor & Eton Riverside (55 min direct, slightly cheaper, £11-£15) — but NOTE contactless does NOT work yet on this route; (3) book tickets ONLY at gwr.com, swrailway.com, or trainline.com — never via third-party 'Windsor Rail + Castle' aggregators; (4) apply UK Senior Railcard (£30/year, age 60+) for 34% discount — applies to both routes; (5) at Windsor, both stations are in the town center — Central is next to Windsor Castle, Riverside is 400m away by the river; (6) refuse ALL 'Windsor Rail + Castle' combo packages at £65-£89 — train is £11-£15, Castle is £33.50 (£20 senior), total £44.50-£48.50 direct vs £65-£89 bundle; (7) for Windsor + Hampton Court Palace same-day, the route is London → Windsor (morning) → Clapham Junction → Hampton Court (afternoon) — well-documented on GWR/SWR sites; (8) for Windsor + Legoland same-day, the direct bus 702 runs from Windsor town center to Legoland (£4 single); (9) older travelers with mobility needs: both Windsor stations have step-free access, but Riverside has steeper platform ramps — Central is slightly easier.
scams.avoidance: For contactless tap-and-go: GWR London Paddington → Slough → Windsor & Eton Central For direct-route: SWR London Waterloo → Windsor & Eton Riverside (NO contactless, pre-book) Book tickets ONLY at gwr.com, swrailway.com, or trainline.com Apply UK Senior Railcard (£30/year, age 60+) for 34% discount — both routes Refuse 'Windsor Rail + Castle' combos at £65-£89 — £11-£15 train + £33.50 Castle = £44.50 direct
scams.location: Windsor & Eton Central station, Windsor & Eton Riverside station, Slough junction — targeting tourists unfamiliar with Windsor's two-station setup

scams.name: Legoland Windsor Ticket Reseller & Parking 'Car Park Exit Fiasco'
scams.description: Legoland Windsor (operated by Merlin Entertainments) is one of the UK's largest theme parks and the #2 Windsor tourist destination after Windsor Castle. Official admission is £49-£79 adult (varies by date — peak weekend rates higher) direct at legoland.co.uk, with dynamic pricing and advance booking typically cheaper. Parking is £8 per car (pre-book online). Over 2024-2025 the community has documented a specific pattern of ticket reseller fraud AND a 'car park exit fiasco' where ANPR-enforced private parking operators issue £100+ fines for vaguely-defined violations. Traveler reports document direct ticket resale discussion, the named parking scam ('A day at Windsor ruined by the car park exit fiasco'), and cross-reference confusing ticket requirements. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers (traveling with grandchildren): (1) third-party reseller sites (legoland-tickets.com, windsor-legoland.co.uk and SEO variants) sell tickets at the same £49-£79 face value but add £4-£8 'booking fee' + £2-£5 'seat selection' at checkout, bringing final price to £55-£91 per adult; (2) some resellers sell 'sold out' dates that aren't actually sold out — taking payment, then delivering 'voucher' tickets that fail at the gate; (3) Merlin Attractions offers Merlin Annual Pass at £149-£229 per year that includes Legoland, Alton Towers, Thorpe Park, LEGO Discovery, SEA LIFE, Madame Tussauds — excellent value for families visiting 2+ parks; (4) 'Legoland + Windsor Castle combo' at £79-£139 per person via third parties is rarely a true discount — direct: Legoland £49-£79 + Windsor Castle £33.50 = £82.50-£112.50 adult; (5) the 'car park exit fiasco': the Legoland car park operates via ANPR (automatic number-plate recognition) cameras — if you exit without paying the £8 fee at the pay machine OR your pre-paid booking doesn't register, you receive a £100+ 'Parking Charge Notice' (PCN) from a private enforcement company 2-4 weeks later; (6) older travelers are specifically affected because (a) they may not realize the ANPR system is active, (b) the pay machines malfunction on busy days, (c) they may drive through the exit barriers that have been lifted for previous cars, triggering a fine; (7) the Legoland Windsor parking fine is technically an INVOICE (civil, not criminal) — recipients can appeal via the operator's dispute process, but unfamiliarity with UK ANPR-enforcement law leads many older tourists to pay unnecessarily. For older travelers visiting Legoland Windsor (typically with grandchildren): (1) book tickets ONLY at legoland.co.uk direct — verify the URL manually; (2) for 2+ UK theme-park visits, consider Merlin Annual Pass at £149-£229 (covers Legoland, Alton Towers, Thorpe Park, 11 more attractions); (3) book parking at £8/car via the same legoland.co.uk site — ensure the confirmation email shows your license plate registered; (4) on arrival, confirm you entered your license plate number correctly at the pay machine OR the online booking; (5) exit via the MAIN exit lane and wait for the barrier to lift for YOUR car specifically — don't tailgate the car in front; (6) if you receive a 'Parking Charge Notice' (PCN) 2-4 weeks after visit, DON'T immediately pay — appeal via parkingappeals.co.uk with evidence of your pre-booked parking confirmation; (7) for transport without parking risk, bus 702 from Windsor town center to Legoland (£4 single, £7 day return) — avoids the car park entirely; (8) refuse ALL third-party 'Legoland ticket' booking sites — book direct; (9) decline 'Legoland + Windsor Castle' combos at £79-£139 — book both separately; (10) for older travelers with walking difficulty, Legoland provides free wheelchair/buggy loans — specify at ticket booking.
scams.avoidance: Book tickets ONLY at legoland.co.uk — verify URL manually For 2+ theme-park visits, Merlin Annual Pass at £149-£229 covers Legoland + Alton Towers + Thorpe Park + 11 more Book parking at £8/car via legoland.co.uk with correct license plate If you get a PCN 2-4 weeks later, appeal via parkingappeals.co.uk — don't immediately pay Bus 702 from Windsor town center to Legoland at £4 single avoids the car park entirely
scams.location: Legoland Windsor Resort (Winkfield Road, Windsor), Legoland Windsor car park — targeting family travelers and tourists combining Windsor + Legoland same-day

scams.name: Windsor + Stonehenge + Bath Coach-Park Combo Day-Trip Fraud
scams.description: Windsor is frequently marketed as 'one leg' of a multi-city London day-trip combo alongside Stonehenge, Bath, and sometimes Hampton Court Palace. These combo products are the most-booked UK day-tour category and generate the largest tourist-dollar volume — they're also the most-criticized product category per UK travel community consensus. This scam pattern is closely related to the Bath Batch-1 coach-tour scam but treated as a Windsor-origin issue here because Windsor is where the individual-destination choice collapses. Traveler reports widely document the pattern, naming the multi-city day-trip as the top tourist mistake and covering both 2025 specific combo variants and the Hampton Court + Windsor combo variant. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers (Windsor-specific): (1) the 'Windsor external only' pattern — many combo tours include Windsor in the 'external viewing' category (photos from the Long Walk, no interior State Apartments); (2) Windsor Castle admission (£33.50) is NOT included in the coach-tour price unless explicitly listed — older tourists discover at the castle that interior access requires separate £33.50 per person; (3) 'Windsor + Changing of the Guard' combos claim 'exclusive Guard view' that is actually the free public pavement; (4) Hampton Court + Windsor same-day is possible but tight — each site needs 3+ hours for meaningful visit, plus 1h transit between them — combo tours typically give 1.5h each; (5) the 'Windsor + Stonehenge + Bath' 3-city combo crams Windsor into 30-45 min (insufficient for any meaningful exploration); (6) coach-tour pickup times are typically 7:30-8:00 AM from London Victoria — older travelers on jet-lag from the US struggle with this early start and miss the first pickup; (7) return to London is 20:00-22:00 — a 14-hour door-to-door day; (8) cancellation policies are often 'non-refundable within 48 hours' — catching tourists who need to change plans; (9) the 'Windsor coach park drop' is typically at Windsor Coach Park, 400m from the castle — the Long Walk is 1.5 miles from the coach park, making 'Long Walk photo stop' requires bus or taxi add-on that's not in the itinerary. For older travelers considering Windsor as a London day-trip: (1) pick Windsor or pick Stonehenge — don't combine both in one day; (2) for Windsor ALONE: train London Waterloo to Windsor & Eton Riverside (55 min direct, £11-£15) OR London Paddington to Windsor & Eton Central (via Slough, £9-£14) — spend a full day seeing Castle, Long Walk, St George's Chapel; (3) if you want to combine Windsor + one other site: Windsor + Hampton Court is the most-feasible same-day combo (both are on Thames within 30 min by train) — each site needs 2-3 hours; (4) refuse 'Windsor + Stonehenge + Bath' 3-city combos at £99-£145 per person — Windsor allocation is too short for meaningful visit; (5) for the 'external Windsor only' budget experience, the Windsor town center + Long Walk + Changing of the Guard on a day without castle admission can be done in 4-5 hours for £25-£40 — don't pay £99-£145 for the same thing via a coach tour; (6) for Windsor Castle INCLUDED properly in a combo: Rabbie's Tours or Evan Evans 'Windsor + Stonehenge' (2-city, not 3) at £129-£159 per person IS better value than 3-city combos; (7) for older travelers with mobility concerns, a single-destination Windsor day is vastly less physically taxing than a 3-city coach marathon; (8) use UK Senior Railcard (£30/year, 60+) for 34% off direct train fares; (9) if booking a coach tour, confirm 24-hr refund window and check what 'Windsor included' actually means (external only, castle admission separate, Long Walk stop, Changing of the Guard view, etc.).
scams.avoidance: Pick Windsor OR Stonehenge — don't combine three sites in one London day-trip For Windsor alone: train Waterloo → Windsor & Eton Riverside (55 min, £11-15) + Castle £33.50 If combo, Windsor + Hampton Court (both on Thames, 30 min apart) is the most-feasible same-day If coach tour, use Rabbie's or Evan Evans 2-city Windsor + Stonehenge (not 3-city combos) UK Senior Railcard (£30/year, age 60+) = 34% off all direct train fares
scams.location: London Victoria Coach Station, London Paddington pickup — targeting the Windsor/Stonehenge/Bath/Hampton-Court combination day-trip market

scams.name: Windsor Castle Hill Tourist-Trap Cafes & Thames Pier Boat Upsell
scams.description: Windsor town's Castle Hill and Windsor High Street — the streets running from Windsor Castle main entrance to the Thames Promenade — have a concentrated tourist-trap restaurant and cafe corridor calibrated for one-time post-castle-visit meals. One local verdict: 'Windsor... Has good pubs, tourist trap shops and a castle.' Additionally, Thames Promenade pier-side operators sell Thames boat tours at significant markup via touts — traveler reports document some tours booked at £160 per person that should be £25-£45. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers: (1) Castle Hill and High Street restaurants are positioned within 200 metres of the Windsor Castle exit — maximum tourist flow, priced at £22-£35 for pub-standard food (legitimate Windsor pub pricing is £14-£22); (2) 'Windsor castle-view' restaurants add £3-£5 premium for outdoor seating with castle views — rarely worth the uplift; (3) the Crooked House Tea Room (52 High Street) and Windsor's branded 'King's Cafe' establishments often appear in coach-tour-recommended lists with 10-15% kickback to tour guides; (4) Thames Promenade boat tour touts at the pier sell 'Windsor-Maidenhead Thames cruise' at £25-£45 per person for 60-90 minute trips — decent value IF it's the licensed French Brothers Ltd boat tour (frenchbrothers.co.uk, the main operator); (5) 'Windsor Luxury Thames Cruise' at £160 per person via third parties bundles a 60-min boat + 'champagne' + 'castle photo opportunity' — the actual cost stack is £25-£35 boat + £15 champagne, so you're overpaying £110-£120; (6) 'Thames River Cruise + Windsor Castle + Wine Tasting' combos at £189-£299 via aggregators similarly bundle at 2-3x individual costs; (7) older travelers are particularly affected at the pier because the tout pitch catches them right after the emotionally-charged Windsor Castle visit, in the 'I want to extend this' mode; (8) legitimate French Brothers Thames Cruise from Windsor runs every 40 min, 2 hours, at £18-£28 adult — the community-recommended baseline; (9) Runnymede (where Magna Carta was signed, 5 miles downstream from Windsor) is accessible by combining the French Brothers boat + a short bus ride, but 'Magna Carta Trail' coach-tour bundles at £79-£129 are marked up 2-3x. For older travelers looking for Windsor food and Thames boat experiences: (1) skip Castle Hill and High Street sit-down restaurants for main meals — walk 3-5 minutes to community-recommended Windsor venues: The Two Brewers (Park Street, £16-£24 mains), The Carpenters Arms (Market Street, £14-£22 mains), or The Bell & Dragon at Cookham (if you're combining with a Thames outing, £22-£32); (2) for casual lunch, the Windsor Market Square food vendors (below the castle on Peascod Street) offer £6-£12 lunches; (3) for cream tea with a view, Crooked House Tea Room (52 High Street, £14-£18 cream tea, historic building) is genuine if pricey; (4) for Thames boat tours, book French Brothers (frenchbrothers.co.uk, £18-£28 adult for 2-hour Windsor cruise) — the established licensed operator; (5) refuse ALL 'Windsor Luxury Thames Cruise' offers at £160+ from pier touts — you're paying 3-5x the legitimate rate; (6) decline 'Thames River Cruise + Windsor Castle + Wine Tasting' combos — book each separately; (7) for the Magna Carta connection, the direct route to Runnymede is French Brothers boat to Runnymede (5 miles, 90 min, £15-£22 one-way) — cheaper and more scenic than coach tours; (8) verify your Thames boat tour operator is French Brothers Ltd (the main Windsor licensed operator) — unlicensed 'Thames cruise' pitches at the pier are the issue; (9) for older travelers with mobility concerns, the French Brothers boats have wheelchair access — specify at booking.
scams.avoidance: For Windsor pub meals: The Two Brewers (£16-£24), The Carpenters Arms (£14-£22), The Bell & Dragon (£22-32) For casual lunch, Windsor Market Square food vendors on Peascod Street at £6-£12 For Thames boat tours, book French Brothers at frenchbrothers.co.uk (£18-£28 adult, 2-hour cruise) Refuse 'Windsor Luxury Thames Cruise' at £160+ — you're paying 3-5x legitimate rate For Magna Carta at Runnymede, take French Brothers boat (£15-£22 one-way, 90 min) not a coach tour
scams.location: Castle Hill + Windsor High Street restaurants (adjacent to Windsor Castle), Windsor Promenade Thames boat pier — targeting post-castle-visit tourists
